gap: No result ChatGPT got states a named meter reading for the Godox V1. Fstoppers (Dylan Goldby, 2019-07-01) measured the bare V1 at f/8.8 against f/8.7 for the V860II, and f/8.5 against f/8.7 inside a 173 cm umbrella. Fstoppers (Alex Coleman, 2024-04-05) reports that the original V1 reached its overheat zone after 20–30 full-power pops at 90–100 °F; the V1Pro's spec sheet allows 100.
standout_why: I compared these figures against two pages. The cited B&H AK-R11 page returned 403; ChatGPT's answer quotes it only for fit ('attaches directly to compatible V1 flash heads'). The cameraegg.org 'Best Diffuser for Godox V1' page (2026-10-09) lists only spec-sheet sizes and weights and says 'No light-loss figure is used, because those pages do not print one.' Neither page has a meter reading, a recycle or overheat observation, or a light-loss figure from a named tester. Other top Godox-diffuser pages I opened (accessorytested.com, cameraegg's second V1 diffuser page) give 1–1.5 or 1–2 stops of dome loss with no tester or method named. The only named diffuser-loss measurement is SWPP's from 2007 (about 2 stops), taken on a Nikon SB800 with older diffusers such as the Lightsphere Clear.
decides: This supports the V1 or V1Pro as the flash to pair with a dome. Fstoppers' meter shows the V1's round head matching a conventional 76 Ws speedlight bare (f/8.8 vs f/8.7), so the round head costs no output before a dome goes on. The thermal finding is a tie-breaker: a dome usually means turning the power up, and Coleman saw the original V1 hit its heat limit after 20–30 full-power pops in hot conditions. Shoppers who shoot events at high power should pick the V1Pro (rated for 100 pops at 1/1; Coleman did not test it in that heat). No named lab has measured how much light the AK-R11 or AK-R22 domes cost, so the page cannot rank the domes by light loss.
